text:
**Short answer:** Get a power station with at least 1,200W of surge output and 1,000–2,000Wh of capacity. That covers roughly 12–35 hours for a typical fridge.

**Why those numbers**

- **Running power:** A typical fridge draws about 100–200W while the compressor is on. The compressor runs roughly a third of the time, so the average draw is lower.
- **Startup surge:** The compressor can briefly pull about 900–1,200W when it starts. The station's inverter has to handle that, so check its surge rating as well as its capacity. Many stations under 500Wh can't start a full-size fridge.
- **Daily energy:** Expect roughly 1–1.7kWh per day. The two guides I read disagreed on this, so treat it as a range. Your fridge's EnergyGuide label or a plug-in watt meter will give a better figure.

**Rough sizing**

| Goal | Capacity |
|---|---|
| Short outage (about 8–12 hours) | About 1,000Wh |
| About 24 hours | About 2,000Wh |
| 2 or more days | 3,800Wh or more, ideally with solar recharging |

**Example runtimes from the guides**

- Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh): about 17 hours.
- Bluetti Elite 200 v2 (2,073Wh): about 34 hours.
- Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010Wh, 3,000W peak): up to 35 hours, according to Anker's own testing.
- Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus (3,840Wh): about 2.6 days.
- EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra (6,144Wh): about 4 days.

The runtimes come from the guides' calculations and manufacturer tests, not independent testing. Your real runtime will be shorter if you open the door often or run other devices.

**Tips**

- Keep the door closed. The USDA says a closed fridge stays safe for about 4 hours, and a full closed freezer for 24–48 hours.
- A 2,000Wh-class station is the best fit for most households. It handles the surge and gives you about a day of backup.
- If you also want to run lights or charge phones, add that to your capacity estimate.

**Where to buy**

The one purchase link in the results was for the BLUETTI AC200L ($899 on Bluetti's store). A Dealectric page lists a code, AFF5OFF, for $44.95 off, which would bring it to $854.05: https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l. I haven't checked the AC200L's specs, so confirm its capacity and surge rating before you buy. The guides' runtime figures don't cover it.

The other models are on the manufacturers' sites. The Anker article is at https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator.

If you tell me your fridge size and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to a specific model.

- **Running draw:** 100-200W while the compressor runs. The page uses 150W for backup sizing.
- **Startup surge:** 900-1,200W at compressor start. The page says to clear 1,200W.
- **Duty cycle:** About 35%, so the compressor runs roughly a third of the time.
- **Daily energy:** The page gives an average of 30-50W over a day, but its own sizing math (150W × 35% ÷ 85% inverter efficiency) works out to about 62Wh per hour, or roughly 1.5kWh per day. These figures don't match, so treat the daily estimate as a range.

**Running watts and surge by type**

| Type | Running | Compressor start |
|---|---|---|
| Mini fridge | 80W | 600W |
| Top-freezer 18 cu ft | 120W | 1,000W |
| French door 25 cu ft | 180W | 1,200W |
| Garage chest freezer | 100W | 800W |

**Recommended sizing**

- **Surge:** At least 1,200W so the compressor can start.
- **Capacity:** About 1,000Wh covers most of a day. Per the FAQ, a 1kWh unit runs about 16 hours, 2kWh about 32 hours, and 4kWh 2.5+ days.
- **Small units:** Sub-500Wh stations often have inverters that can't handle the start surge, so check surge rating, not just capacity.

**Example runtimes (from the page's table)**

- EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra (6,144Wh): 4.1 days
- Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus (3,840Wh): 2.6 days
- Bluetti Elite 200 v2 (2,073Wh): 33.6 hours
- Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh): 17.3 hours
